critical computational challenges when handling large-scale matrix inversions and solving substantial linear system problems, prompting significant research into rapid matrix inversion methods via GPU-accelerated techniques. Among these, the Fully Factorized Method (FFM) and the Block Diagonal Method (BDM) demonstrate notable efficacy and scalability. However, although BDM benefits from a simpler structure compared to FFM—resulting in faster precomputation and forward/backward solving phases—it suffers from a less accurate initial diagonalization. Conversely, BDM's ability to employ highly optimized, large-scale solvers for its diagonal blocks offers a strong advantage. Comprehensive experiments on massive matrices demonstrate that the proposed Adaptive BDM delivers a favorable balance, delivering both high computational efficiency and high numerical accuracy.
